applies_to: the raw bytes of JCS(statement), the bytes the content-address is computed over

derivation.max_statement_bytes: 2 * 2592 + 1024 = 6208. 2592 bytes is the largest public key among the families this profile admits (ML-DSA-87, FIPS 204; ML-DSA-44/65 are 1312/1952 bytes, every SLH-DSA (FIPS 205) parameter set is at most 64), carried as hex in pq_pubkey, so 5184 bytes. 1024 bytes covers every other member: the largest non-key overhead among the published statements is 313 bytes (the SLH-DSA rotation statement), so 1024 is chosen headroom, not a measured maximum.
derivation.max_member_name_escaped_bytes: 64 escaped bytes per member name. The longest published member name is 27 bytes (predecessor_content_address). The bound is what makes the member-ordering rule decidable from a fixed window, which an on-chain segment fraud proof needs.

admission: A statement whose bytes exceed max_statement_bytes MUST be rejected at admission, before it is anchored or accepted; the size bound is checked against the raw byte length alone, so this is unconditional and chain-enforceable. A statement with any member name longer than max_member_name_escaped_bytes in escaped form MUST be rejected at admission, or refuted by a bounded fraud proof within the challenge window -- the name bound is a property of canonical form (JCS member ordering), so an implementation MAY defer it to the same fraud proof canonical form itself relies on, inheriting that proof's one-honest-watcher assumption rather than the size bound's unconditional one.
governs: Statements that declare profile pq_key_binding.v1 (or a later profile that references this facet by the same derivation). A statement declaring pq_key_binding.v0, or carrying no profile tag, is outside this facet's scope -- v0 is the frozen base this facet refines, not a second conformance target. The pq_key_binding.v0 cases in the vector corpus (published_kya-*) are kept as non-normative regression evidence that the bound excludes nothing already anchored under v0, not a claim that v0 statements are themselves bound by it.
scope: Canonical form only. This facet does not change the cutoff rule, the content-address, or in-force resolution.
versioning: Per profile and versioned. A profile that admits a family with a larger public key declares its own facet with the same derivation; it never amends this one.
